CampaignSendResult.description:
Per-recipient result returned synchronously after the trigger request.
Accepted recipients are queued for delivery; check the send status endpoint
for delivery confirmation.

handle.description: Delivery address of the recipient, present for inline (`handle`) recipients.

id.description:
Primary key of the recipient as configured on the Personalization API sync,
present for profile (`id`) recipients.

status.description: Whether this recipient was accepted for delivery or rejected at validation time.

sendId.description:
Unique identifier for this send, present when `status` is `"accepted"`.
Use with `POST /campaigns/{id}/sends/batch-get` to poll for delivery
status; it accepts up to 100 `sendId` values per request.

reason.description:
Reason for rejection, present when `status` is `"rejected"`.
- `invalid_handle` — the delivery address is not a valid email or phone number
- `missing_variables` — one or more required template variables are absent
  (`handle` recipients only; `id` recipients are checked at send time)
- `invalid_id` — the profile ID is empty or missing
- `missing_handle_or_id` — the recipient has neither `handle` nor `id`
- `invalid_locale` — the `locale` is empty or longer than 7 characters
- `whatsapp_marketing_us_number` — the message uses a marketing WhatsApp template, which Meta does not deliver to US phone numbers

missingVariables.description:
Names of the required template variables absent from the recipient's data,
present when `reason` is `"missing_variables"`.

StartCampaignResponse.description:
Response body for a campaign trigger request. Results are returned in the
same order as the input `recipients` array.

results.description:
Per-recipient outcomes. Accepted recipients are queued for delivery;
rejected recipients were not sent.

TriggerErrorResponse.description:
Body returned on a request-level failure (400/404/409/429) so the caller
knows why the request was rejected.

error.description: Human-readable description of why the request failed.

HandleCampaignRecipient.description:
A recipient identified by their delivery address (email or phone number).
Personalization data is provided inline in the request.

handle.description:
Delivery address for this recipient. Must be a valid email address for
email campaigns, or an E.164-formatted phone number for SMS and WhatsApp campaigns.

properties.description:
Per-recipient personalization properties. Keys must match the variable
names shown in the message editor. These are merged with the top-level
`properties` and take precedence when a key appears in both.

locale.description:
The recipient's locale as a BCP 47 language tag, such as `es-ES`, matched
against the locales the message is localized into (case-insensitive). When
omitted, the recipient gets the message's source language. A locale the
message is not localized into follows the workspace's localization fallback
setting. At most 7 characters.

ProfileCampaignRecipient.description:
A recipient identified by their Personalization API Cached profile ID.
Template variables are checked at send time, after the cached profile is
merged with `properties`. A required variable (one without a Liquid default)
missing from both drops the send, which the send status endpoint reports as
`dropped`. A variable present with a null or empty value renders blank.

id.description:
Primary key of the recipient as configured on the Personalization API sync.
The delivery address is resolved from the cache at send time.

properties.description:
Per-recipient personalization overrides. Merged with the top-level
`properties` and the cached profile; these values take precedence when a
key appears in multiple sources.

locale.description:
The recipient's locale as a BCP 47 language tag, such as `es-ES`, matched
against the locales the message is localized into (case-insensitive). When
omitted, the recipient gets the message's source language. A locale the
message is not localized into follows the workspace's localization fallback
setting. At most 7 characters.

CampaignRecipient.description:
A single send target. Provide either `handle` (inline delivery address) or
`id` (Personalization API profile ID), but not both.

StartCampaignRequest.description: Request body for triggering an API campaign send.

properties.description:
Shared personalization properties applied to all recipients. Keys must
match the variable names shown in the message editor. Per-recipient
`properties` take precedence when a key appears in both.

draft.description:
When `true`, sends the campaign even if it has not been activated.
Intended for test sends against draft campaigns only.

recipients.description:
List of recipients to send to. Each entry must include either a `handle`
(delivery address) or an `id` (Personalization API based profile ID).

SendStatus.description:
Delivery status of a send. `not_found` means no send with this id exists on
the campaign, including a send that has not been processed yet.

SendStatusReasonCode.description:
Stable machine-readable reason a send was dropped or failed. Branch on this
value; the wording of `reason` may change.

BatchSendStatusResult.description: Delivery status for one requested send.

sendId.description: The `sendId` this result is for, echoed from the request.

reason.description:
Readable explanation for why this send was dropped or failed. Present
when `status` is `"dropped"` or `"failed"`.

reasonCode.description: Stable code for `reason`. Present whenever `reason` is.

updatedAt.description:
ISO 8601 time the status last changed. Absent when `status` is
`"not_found"`.

BatchSendStatusResponse.description:
Response body for the batch send status endpoint. Results are returned in the
same order as the requested `sendIds`.

BatchSendStatusRequest.description: Request body for the batch send status endpoint.

sendIds.description: `sendId` values returned by the trigger endpoint.

CreateSignupResponse.description:
`subscribed` means consent settled in this request. `doi_pending_confirmation`
means a confirmation was sent and consent settles when the person answers,
which may be days later.

SignupChannel.description: Delivery channels a signup can consent on.

SignupTraitsRequest.description:
A signup's own fields, as collected by the form. They are written to the
customer's warehouse and never stored by Hightouch.

optIn.description:
Force an opt-in style. Omit to let the topic and channel decide; a value
they cannot honor is refused rather than silently resolved.

source.description: Which form or landing page this signup came from.

topicId.description:
The subscription topic being consented to, by id or external identifier.
Omit both to record consent for the channel itself.

handle.description: Email address or E.164 phone number, matching `channel`.

AudienceSizeJob.description: The status of an audience size job.

status.description:
"pending": The job is running
"success": The job is finished
"failed": The job could not be completed
"cancelled": The job was cancelled before it finished

size.description: The size of the audience. Set if `status` is "success".

evaluatedAt.description: The timestamp when the job finished. Set if `status` is "success".

error.description: The reason the job failed. Set if `status` is "failed".

DecisionEngineMessageGuardrails.description: Guardrail fields on a message (max sends, eligibility dates, etc.)

DecisionEngineVariableVariant.description: Variant within a message variable (Public API)

value.description: The default (non-localized) value for this variant

tags.description: Key-value tags for categorizing this variant

firstEligibleSendDate.description: Earliest date this variant is eligible to be sent (ISO 8601)

lastEligibleSendDate.description: Latest date this variant is eligible to be sent (ISO 8601)

localeValues.description:
Localized values for this variant, keyed by locale code (e.g. "en-US", "de-DE").
These are only used at runtime when `localizationEnabled` is true on the parent variable.
You can stage translations by providing localeValues while leaving localizationEnabled unset or false.

name.description: The variable name (must be unique within a message)

localizationEnabled.description:
When true, the Decision Engine uses each variant's localeValues to select
locale-appropriate content at runtime. When false or omitted, only the
default variant value is used, even if localeValues are present.

maxSendsPerUserWindowDays.description: Rolling window in days for the maxSendsPerUser limit

maxSendsPerUser.description: Maximum number of times this variable's variants can be sent to a single user

id.description: The component's id. Omit when creating. On update, a component matches an existing one by id when supplied, otherwise by (name, version); include the id to rename a component in place.

fullRerun.description: Whether to resync the entire Identity Graph or process incrementally.

TriggerRunIdrInput.description: The input of a trigger action to run IDR.

numSourceRows.description: The exact number of rows processed from sources in this run.

numNewUniqueProfiles.description: The exact number of unique profiles in the graph created during this run.

numUniqueProfiles.description: The exact number of unique profiles in the graph at the end of the run.

stats.description: If available, the stats at the end of a successful run.

finishedAt.description: Timestamp of the run's completion. Only set for successful or failed runs.

startedAt.description: Timestamp of the run's start. Not set for queued runs.

error.description: If available, the error associated with a failed status.

ListIdrRunsOutput.description: The output of a request to list runs for an IDR graph.

requestId.description: ID associated with the reprocessing request. This can be used to query the status of the request.

identifiers.description:
e.g. [{ identifier: "email", value: "a@b.com" }]
Identifier values will be queued for reprocessing.
Clusters containing these identifiers will be reprocessed on the next run.

block.description: If true, identifier values will also be added to the blocklist and ignored in future runs.

status.description:
"queueing": The identifiers are being queued for reprocessing.
"queued": The identifiers have been queued and added to the blocklist. Their associated clusters will be reprocessed next time the graph runs.
"reprocessed": The identifiers' clusters have been reprocessed during a run.
"failed": We failed to queue the identifiers for reprocessing.
"cancelled": The reprocessing request has been cancelled.

queuedAt.description: Set if the status is "queued" or "reprocessed". The timestamp when the identifiers were queued for reprocessing.

reprocessedAt.description: Set if the status is "reprocessed". The timestamp when the identifiers' clusters were reprocessed.

reprocessedRunId.description: Set if the status is "reprocessed". The ID of the run that reprocessed the identifiers' clusters.

recordFound.description:
One result per identifier, in the order they were submitted.
True if the identifier was found in the graph at the start of the run that processed the request.
Null until the request is processed, and on requests submitted before this field existed on the API.

error.description: If available, the error message from failing to queue the identifiers for reprocessing.

Sync.description:
Syncs define how data from models are mapped to destinations. Each time a
sync runs, Hightouch calculates the rows that have changed since the last
run, and syncs them to Sync's destination.

slug.description: The sync's slug

workspaceId.description: The id of the workspace that the sync belongs to

createdAt.description: The timestamp when the sync was created

updatedAt.description: The timestamp when the sync was last updated

createdBy.description: The user who created the sync, or null if no user was recorded

updatedBy.description: The user who last updated the sync, or null if no user was recorded

destinationId.description: The id of the Destination that sync is connected to

modelId.description: The id of the Model that sync is connected to

configuration.description:
The sync's configuration. This specifies how data is mapped, among other
configuration.

The schema depends on the destination type.

For a sync bound to a sync template this is the effective configuration:
the template's configuration with this sync's `syncTemplateOverrides`
applied.

Consumers should NOT make assumptions on the contents of the
configuration. It may change as Hightouch updates its internal code.

schedule.description:
The scheduling configuration. It can be triggered based on several ways:

Interval: the sync will be triggered based on certain interval(minutes/hours/days/weeks)

Cron: the sync will be triggered based on cron expression https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cron.

Visual: the sync will be triggered based a visual cron configuration on UI

DBT-cloud: the sync will be triggered based on a dbt cloud job

Match Booster (type "match_booster"): the sync will be triggered after each
Match Booster enrichment run of its model completes. Requires the model to
have Match Booster enabled, and takes no inner schedule payload.

status.description: The overall status of the sync

disabled.description: Whether the sync has been disabled by the user.

lastRunAt.description: The timestamp of the last sync run

referencedColumns.description: The reference column that sync depends on to sync data from source

primaryKey.description: The primary key that sync uses to identify data from source

externalSegment.description: The user facing ID for any created lists or audiences in the sync destination

syncTemplateId.description:
The id of the sync template this sync is bound to, or null when the sync
owns its configuration. A bound sync takes its destination and
configuration from the template and follows later changes to the
template; `configuration` is the effective merged configuration and
`syncTemplateOverrides` holds this sync's own values.

syncTemplateOverrides.description:
The template configuration fields this sync overrides, keyed by
configuration field path (for example "externalIdMapping" or
"target.schema"). Null when the sync is not bound to a sync template or
has no overrides.

SyncCreate.description:
The input for creating a Sync.

A sync either owns its configuration (`destinationId` and `configuration`
are required) or is created from a sync template (`syncTemplateId` is
required, `configuration` must be omitted and this sync's own values go in
`syncTemplateOverrides`).

slug.description: The sync's slug

modelId.description: The id of the Model that sync is connected to

schedule.description:
The scheduling configuration. It can be triggered based on several ways:

Interval: the sync will be triggered based on certain interval(minutes/hours/days/weeks)

Cron: the sync will be triggered based on cron expression https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cron.

Visual: the sync will be triggered based a visual cron configuration on UI

DBT-cloud: the sync will be triggered based on a dbt cloud job

Match Booster (type "match_booster"): the sync will be triggered after each
Match Booster enrichment run of its model completes. Requires the model to
have Match Booster enabled, and takes no inner schedule payload.

disabled.description: Whether the sync has been disabled by the user.

destinationId.description:
The id of the Destination that sync is connected to. Required unless
`syncTemplateId` is provided: a sync created from a sync template always
uses the template's destination, and this field, when provided, must
match it.

configuration.description:
The sync's configuration. This specifies how data is mapped, among other
configuration. The schema depends on the destination type.

Required unless `syncTemplateId` is provided, in which case it must be
omitted: the template provides the configuration and this sync's own
values go in `syncTemplateOverrides`.

syncTemplateId.description:
The id of the Sync Template to create the sync from. The sync inherits
the template's destination and configuration and follows later changes
to the template. A null `schedule` inherits the template's schedule; a
schedule given here belongs to the sync. `modelId` must be the template's
model or an audience built on it.

syncTemplateOverrides.description:
Values this sync sets for the template's overridable fields, keyed by
configuration field path (for example "externalIdMapping" or
"target.schema"). Only fields the template's `overrideConfig` marks as
overridable are accepted. Requires `syncTemplateId`.

SyncUpdate.description: The input for updating a Sync

configuration.description:
The sync's configuration. This specifies how data is mapped, among other
configuration.

The schema depends on the destination type.

For a sync bound to a sync template this is the effective configuration:
the template's configuration with this sync's `syncTemplateOverrides`
applied.

Consumers should NOT make assumptions on the contents of the
configuration. It may change as Hightouch updates its internal code.

schedule.description:
The scheduling configuration. It can be triggered based on several ways:

Interval: the sync will be triggered based on certain interval(minutes/hours/days/weeks)

Cron: the sync will be triggered based on cron expression https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cron.

Visual: the sync will be triggered based a visual cron configuration on UI

DBT-cloud: the sync will be triggered based on a dbt cloud job

Match Booster (type "match_booster"): the sync will be triggered after each
Match Booster enrichment run of its model completes. Requires the model to
have Match Booster enabled, and takes no inner schedule payload.

disabled.description: Whether the sync has been disabled by the user.

syncTemplateId.description:
The id of a Sync Template to bind the sync to, or null to detach the sync
from its template. Binding requires the template's destination to match
the sync's destination; while bound, the sync follows the template's
configuration and `configuration` cannot be set directly. Detaching
copies the sync's effective configuration, schedule and other inherited
settings onto the sync so it keeps running unchanged.

syncTemplateOverrides.description:
Replaces the sync's template overrides, keyed by configuration field
path. Only fields the template's `overrideConfig` marks as overridable
are accepted; null clears every override. Requires the sync to be, or to
become, bound to a sync template.

createdAt.description:
The timestamp when sync run was created. In most cases this will be
equivalent to `startedAt`, but it may be earlier if the sync was triggered
while a run was already in progress, and the new run didn't start for
a while.

startedAt.description: The timestamp when the sync run started

finishedAt.description: The timestamp when the sync run finished

querySize.description: The number of rows in the query.

completionRatio.description: The completion ratio of sync run, showing the progress of a sync run

plannedRows.description:
The number of planned rows that this sync run was supposed to execute.

Note that the counts for `successfulRows` and `failedRows` may not add up
to `plannedRows` if the sync was cancelled.

successfulRows.description: The number of rows that were successfully processed by the destination.

failedRows.description:
The number of rows that we attempted to sync, but were rejected by the
destination.

This does not include rows that weren't attempted due to the sync being
cancelled.

error.description: Error message if the sync run didn't finish successfully

resetCDC.description: Whether to sync all the rows in the query without executing changes on the destination.

fullResync.description:

synced rows).

post.description: Start an API-triggered campaign: send to the given recipients.

Get the delivery status of up to 100 sends in a single request, using the
`sendId` values returned from the start endpoint. Prefer this over polling
the single-send endpoint once per `sendId`.

Record a signup: consent for a delivery handle, plus the fields the form
collected.

Whether consent settles immediately or waits for a double opt-in
confirmation is the channel's configuration, so one call covers both and
the response says which happened.

Create a new sync

A sync either owns its configuration (`destinationId` and
`configuration`) or is created from a sync template (`syncTemplateId`).
A sync created from a template uses the template's destination and
configuration, and may set the fields the template's `overrideConfig`
marks as overridable through `syncTemplateOverrides`. The effective
configuration is validated for the destination either way, and
`configuration.<field>` errors on a template sync refer to that merged
configuration.

Approve a sync draft and apply its change. Fails with 409 and applies
nothing when the draft or the sync changed after the versions you send.

Reject a sync draft. The draft closes without applying its change; to try
again, the requester edits the sync.

Trigger a new run for the given sync sequence.

A sequence never runs concurrently with itself. If a run is already in
progress, then where run queueing is enabled for the workspace, a single
follow-up run is queued and starts after the current run completes
(repeated triggers return the same queued run); otherwise the id of the
run already in progress is returned.
